questions.question: Three men or five women can do a work in 57 days. In how many days can nine men and four women do that same work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Three men or five women can do a work in 57 days

**Formula used:**

(M1 × D1)/W1 = (M2 × D2)/W2

**Calculation:**

3 Men = 5 women

1 man = (5/3) women

9 Men = 9 × (5/3) women = 15 women

Total work = 5 × 57 = 285 units

9 men and 4 women = 15 women + 4 women = 19 women

Time taken = 285 ÷ 19 = 15 days

**∴ The nine men and four women will do the same work in 15 days.**

questions.question: It is given that Δ ABC ≅ Δ FDE and AB = 5 cm. ∠B = 40° and ∠A = 80°. Then which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Δ ABC ≅ Δ FDE

AB = 5 cm, ∠B = 40° and ∠A = 80°

**Concept used:**

Two triangles are said to be congruent if their sides have the same length and their angles have the same measure. Thus, two triangles can be superimposed side to side and angle to angle.

**Calculation:**

As Δ ABC ≅ Δ FDE,

AB = DF = 5 cm

∠A = ∠F = 80°

∠B = ∠D = 40°

∠C = ∠E = 180° - 80° - 40° = 60°

**∴ The required answer is Option 4.**

questions.question:
Simplify the given expression.

sqrt (1 + cos P)/(1 - cos P)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

sqrt (1 + cos P)/(1 - cos P)

**Concept used:**

a² - b² = (a + b)(a - b)

1 - cos²θ = sin²θ

**Calculation:**

sqrt (1 + cos P)/(1 - cos P)

⇒ sqrt ((1 + cos P)times(1 + cos P))/((1 - cos P)times(1 + cos P)) 

⇒ sqrt ((1 + cos P)²)/(1 - cos² P) 

⇒ sqrt ((1 + cos P)²)/(sin² P) 

⇒ ((1 + cos P))/(sin P) 

⇒ (1)/(sin P) + (cos P)/(sin P) 

⇒ cosec P + cot P

**∴ The required answer is cosec P + cot P.**

questions.question: Two circles touch each other internally. Their radii are 3 cm and 4 cm. What is the length of the biggest chord of the circle with radii 4 cm which is outside the inner circle?
questions.solution:
Given:

Two circles touch each other internally.

The radius of the inner circle = 3 cm

The radius of the outer circle = 4 cm

**Concept used:**

When two circles are touch each other internally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a92ef9f5aaba595f851324c4c2d592b700849ddb68fcebcdbf27bbff1cd82e8.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4cf8598b36fb0aa6b3f3cd504c8f27f3bce39a376be2c6c56d7e97dfd761c0c1.png] 

When the largest chord of bigger circle is tangent to the inner circle (smaller circle).

Then, 

Radius of inner circle (PD) = x cm

Radius of bigger circle (OB) = y cm

OP = Distance between two centers = Radius of bigger circle - radius of inner circle

⇒OP = y - x

CD = Diameter of inner circle = 2 × (radius of inner circle)

⇒ CD = 2x

OC = Difference between chord and bigger circle centre = CD - PD - OP

OC = CD - PD - OP

⇒ OC = 2x - x - (y - x) = 2x - y

Calculation:

Let the biggest chord of the circle with radii 4 cm which is outside the inner circle = AB

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a92ef9f5aaba595f851324c4c2d592b700849ddb68fcebcdbf27bbff1cd82e8.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4cf8598b36fb0aa6b3f3cd504c8f27f3bce39a376be2c6c56d7e97dfd761c0c1.png] 

From the figure, we know that

PD = 3 cm 

OD = 4 cm

OP = OD - PD

⇒ OP = 4 - 3 = 1 cm

⇒ CD = 2 x PD = 2 x 3 = 6 cm

OC = CD - PD - OP

⇒ OC = 6 - 3 - 1 = 2 cm

⇒ OB = 4 cm = radius of outer circle

By using Pythagoras theorem, we can write that

OB2 = BC2 + OC2

⇒ 42 = BC2 + 22

⇒ BC2 = 16 - 4

⇒ BC2 = 12

⇒ BC = sqrt{12} = 2sqrt{3} cm

Now, 

The length of biggest chord AB = 2 x BC = 2 x 2sqrt{3} = 4sqrt{3} cm

**∴ The length of the biggest chord of the circle outside the inner circle is 4sqrt{3} cm.**

questions.question: In a circular race of 1500 m. Anil and Bilal start from the same point and at the same time with speeds of 36 km/h and 54 km/h respectively. When will they meet again for the first time on the track when they are running in the same direction?
questions.solution:
**Given:** 

The distance of the circular path race = 1500 m

Anil's speed = 36 km/hr

Bilal's speed = 54 km/hr

Both start from the same point and at the same time and run in the same direction.

**Concept used:**

When A and B are moving with x km/hr and y km/hr, respectively

In the same direction,

then Relative speed = (x - y) km/hr

In the opposite direction,

then Relative speed = (x + y) km/hr

**Formula used:**

Conversion of km/hr to m/sec

1 km/hr = (5/18) m/sec

Distance = speed x time

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

They are moving in the same direction,

Relative speed = (54 - 36) km/hr

⇒ Relative speed = 18 km/hr

⇒ Relative speed = 18 x (5/18) m/sec

⇒ Relative speed = 5 m/sec

As we know that,

Distance = Speed x time

⇒ Time = Distance/speed

⇒ Time = 1500/5 = 300 sec

**∴ The answer is 300 sec.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Formula used:

Time taken to meet for the 1st time = Length of the track/Relative Speed

Time taken = L/u+v, when moving in the opposite direction.

Time taken = L/u-v, when moving in the same direction.

Where, L = Length of the track

u = Speed of A, v = speed of B

1 km/hr = (5/18) m/sec

Calculation:

Time taken to meet for the 1st time = 1500/[(54-36) x (5/18)]

So, time taken for meeting for the 1st time = 1500/5 = 300 sec

∴ The answer is 300 sec.

questions.question: A person bought two goods for Rs. 19,500. He sold one at a loss of 20% and the other at a profit of 15%. If the selling price of each goods is the same, find the cost price of goods sold at profit.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A person bought two goods for Rs. 19,500.

**Concept used:**

Selling price = Cost price × (100 + Profit)%

Selling price = Cost price × (100 - Loss)%

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price of two goods be 10x and 10y, respectively

According to the question,

10x × 0.8 = 10y × 1.15

⇒ 8x = 11.5y

⇒ (x/y) = (11.5/8)

Let the value of 'x' and 'y' be 11.5a, and 8a, respectively.

So,

115a + 80a = 19500

⇒ 195a = 19500

⇒ a = 100

So, the cost price of goods sold at profit = 80a = 80 × 100 = 8000

**∴ The required answer is Rs. 8,000.**

questions.question: 65% of Samita's income is equal to 91% of Bhairav's income. If Samita's income was Rs. 1,500 more than what it is and Bhairav's income was Rs. 500 more than what it is, the ratio of the incomes of Samita and Bhairav would have been 3 ∶ 2. What is the actual combined income (in Rs. ) of Samita and Bhairav?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

65 % of Samita's income = 91 % of Bhairav's income

Samita's new income is 1500 more than her current income 

Bhairav's new income is 500 more than her current income

The new ratio of Samita and Bhairav's income = 3 : 2

**Calculation:**

Let Samita's current income = p Rs. and Bhairav's current income = q Rs.

According to the question,

65 % of p = 91 % of q

⇒ 65 × p = 91× q

⇒ p/q = 91/65 = 7/5

Let's assume that ,

⇒Samita's current income (p) = 7k

⇒Bhairav's current income (q) = 5k

Samita's new income = 1500 + Samita' s current income

⇒Samita's new income = 1500 + 7k

Bhairav's new income = 500 + Bhairav's current income

⇒Bhairav's new income = 500 + 5k

The new ratio of incomes of Samita and Bhairav = 3:2

⇒(1500 + 7k)/(500 + 5k) = 3/2

⇒3000 + 14k = 1500 + 15k

⇒ k = 1500

The income of Samita = 7k = 7 x 1500 = 10500 Rs.

The income of Bhairav = 5k = 5 x 1500 = 7500 Rs.

The combined incomes of Samita and Bhairav = 10500 + 7500 = 18000 Rs.

**∴ The Actual combined income of Samita and Bhairav is 18000 Rs.**

questions.question:
Simplify the expression:

(a + b)/(a - b) div ((a + b)²)/((a² - b²))
questions.solution:
**Given:**

**(a + b)/(a - b) div ((a + b)²)/((a² - b²))**

**Concept used:**

a² - b² = (a + b)(a - b)

**Calculation:**

(a + b)/(a - b) div ((a + b)²)/((a² - b²))

⇒ (a + b)/(a - b) times ((a² - b²))/((a + b)²)

⇒ (a + b)/(a - b) times ((a - b)(a + b))/((a + b)²)

⇒ ((a + b))/((a + b))

⇒ 1

**∴ The required answer is 1.**
